subject.title: [Bug]: Performance degradation in session memory sync: full delete-reinsert pattern for growing JSONL files

question: Should OpenClaw pursue incremental session-memory indexing against the current memory_index schema and batching paths, rescue the open candidate PR, or intentionally keep full-entry reindexing for consistency?
rationale: The central bug is source-proven, but the fix direction affects session-state correctness, overlap semantics, source-wide batching, and storage/schema behavior; automation should not choose that product/architecture tradeoff alone.

options.title: Fresh current-main fix
options.body: Implement incremental preservation against the current memory_index schema and source-wide batching paths, with explicit overlap/compaction regression coverage.

options.title: Rescue the open candidate PR
options.body: Ask the contributor or an owner to rebase and replace obsolete assumptions in the existing incremental-sync branch before further review.

options.title: Reject incremental indexing
options.body: Keep full-entry reindexing only if maintainers decide consistency and simpler rebuild semantics outweigh long-session embedding and write overhead.

recommendation.title: Fresh current-main fix
recommendation.body: Implement incremental preservation against the current memory_index schema and source-wide batching paths, with explicit overlap/compaction regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: jalehman owns the adjacent session/transcript storage migration decisions and is best positioned to choose the durable session-state direction.
